workers_per_repo.why: captain 2026-09-02 (decision 3): at most one worker per repo per epic; more than one only when the stories' files_owned are disjoint.
workers_per_repo.review_when: a repo routinely has disjoint-file stories queued behind a single worker.

waves.why: workflow v3 D24 (captain 2026-09-07): the contract lands in the backend story; every client story depends on it.
waves.review_when: a pure-client or pure-docs epic declares waves: single.

context.why: captain 2026-09-08: compaction at 200k wasted time (three in one sdk story); budgets raised to 400k plan / 500k now.
context.review_when: a harness reports usable telemetry showing a different sweet spot.

arena.why: arena v2 (5.2): adversarial review earns its cost only above this bar; below it, arena-lite runs one adversary.
arena.review_when: after several arenas, when the calibration column shows which roles the captain keeps.

delivery.why: workflow v3 (captain 2026-09-02): draft PR at the plan gate, one phase = one commit, push every phase. mode direct-PR (item 8) matches today's behaviour: push + PR, no extra pipeline.
delivery.review_when: a project declares style: pipo (commits stay local, one final push, PR opened ready) or a harder mode (no-mistakes: full gates; local-only: clean ready branch, no push) in its <project>/cox/policy.json.

harness.why: captain 2026-09-15 (decision 8, P9): model-agnostic; the leader is not locked to claude. Bare 'opus' follows worker.models.claude (captain 2026-09-23, B-52: claude workers run claude-opus-5-5; the 2026-09-03 Opus 4.8 ruling is superseded). worker.models is the per-harness default: claude-opus-5-5 for claude, gpt-5.6-sol for codex - M10c, after a codex worker was handed the claude default and rejected the launch; pi is openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol (captain 2026-09-23, B-47/B-48: pi supported fully as claude/codex; pi needs a provider/model, so it carries the provider prefix); worker.model is the legacy claude default, kept readable. launch: a dispatched worker cannot answer a local approval prompt, so it runs autonomously; the captain owns this risk (docs/adapters/{claude,codex}.md).
harness.review_when: a new harness adapter ships a capability card and is added to the options.

routing.review_when: baseline rows >= 12 (3 stories x 2 harnesses x 2 conditions)

merge.why: captain 2026-09-21 (item 8): the captain merges everything. cox ship merge is refused unless --captain runs it, so the green-at-live-head rule is enforced rather than remembered; a worker or leader terminal never merges.
merge.review_when: a project trusts an unattended merge and flips yolo: true in its <project>/cox/policy.json, taking the risk of a non-captain merge.

quota.why: M11 (captain 2026-09-16, option a): observe-only quota. quota-axi (installed binary; npx only via an explicit opt-in with version+integrity) fills coxswain.quota.v1; the leader reroutes by hand. Thresholds are first guesses.

review.why: M13 (captain 2026-09-16): visual review of design/plan/arena artifacts through lavish-axi as an optional external surface (installed binary; npx only via an explicit opt-in with version+integrity). cox owns the artifact and the record; answers go through cox arena answer. share=false because ht-ml.app is a third-party outward-facing host.
review.review_when: after three real reviews, when it is clear whether cox-generated HTML is rich enough or the leader mostly hand-authors per lavish playbooks
